To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have obtained spectroscopy of a microlensing caustic transit of a Galactic bulge K-giant that temporally resolves several phases of the caustic transit and shows that the H alpha equivalent width varies by 30% as the star passes the caustic.

we have temporally resolved the H alpha line profile of a microlensing source during caustic crossing and that the line equivalent width increases slightly at the center of the source star as it crosses the caustic but decreases dramatically during limb crossing.

we have obtained spectroscopy of the source star of a Galactic bulge microlensing event that temporally resolves several phases of the second caustics crossing, including the center and limb of the star, and that we find that the H alpha equivalent width varies by similar to30% as a result of the differential magnification across the face of the star.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the stellar atmospheres of red giant stars in the Galactic bulge, and in particular, with the use of microlensing as a tool to probe their atmospheres.
the study of the stellar structure and dynamics of the central regions of our Galaxy, the Galactic bulge.
the study of the formation and evolution of galaxies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the H alpha EW variation of this microlensed K-giant star is consistent with the predictions of stellar atmosphere models, but the data do not allow a quantitative test.
the H alpha EW variations are not consistent with the stellar model, but that the data are insufficient to rule out the stellar model.

this is the first direct measurement of a stellar surface effect in a microlensed star and the first measurement of differential magnification across the stellar disk of a microlensing event, and it is a direct measurement of the surface gravity and metallicity of a K giant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the microlensing of EROS-BLG-5 provides an unprecedented view of the surface of a giant star and that the observations are qualitatively in agreement with the predictions of stellar atmosphere models.
the H alpha equivalent width is not a good indicator for stellar surface temperature and gravity.
the H alpha equivalent width is a good indicator of the surface gravity and effective temperature of the source star, but it is not a good tracer of the metallicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microlensing can probe the atmospheres of individual stars.
the technique is feasible and can be applied to a variety of stars in the Galactic bulge.
it is feasible to obtain high-resolution spectra during caustic crossings and that these observations will allow the measurement of stellar parameters for a large number of microlensed stars.
